snappy.options.resolution.low_256.desc: Lowest resolution. Fast to capture and very small on disk, but noticeably softer than Minecraft's modern menu backgrounds.
snappy.options.resolution.balanced_512.d: A lightweight middle option. Sharper than 256x256 while still keeping captures quick and files modest.
snappy.options.resolution.default_1024.d: Recommended default. Matches the size used by modern Minecraft menu panoramas and gives a clean background without being excessive.
snappy.options.resolution.very_high_1536: Higher than the normal menu background size. Useful for very large displays, with larger files and a longer capture pause.
snappy.options.resolution.ultra_2048.des: Maximum preset. Best when you want extra-sharp panorama files, but it uses the most memory, disk space, and capture time.
snappy.options.menu_mode.desc: Chooses which panorama is used behind menu screens. If no matching panorama is available, Minecraft's vanilla panorama is shown.
snappy.options.menu_parallax.desc: Gently tilts and turns the menu background panorama toward the mouse cursor.
snappy.options.cycle_interval.desc: How long each panorama stays visible when the menu background mode cycles through multiple panoramas.
snappy.options.cycle_interval.inactive_d: Only used when "Menu Background" is set to a mode that can cycle through multiple panoramas.
snappy.options.hide_hud_normal_screensho: Hides the in-game HUD before saving normal Minecraft screenshots. This only affects normal screenshots; panorama screenshots always hide the HUD. Menus and other open screens are not hidden.
snappy.options.preview_mode.desc: Chooses which screenshot types show a small preview in the top-left corner for 10 seconds after capture.
Shows or hides chat messages from normal and panorama screenshots. Screenshots are still saved either way.
snappy.options.screenshot_browser_button: Shows or hides Snappy's screenshot browser icon on the title screen and pause screen. It opens the screenshot browser.
snappy.options.photo_mode_button.desc: Shows or hides Snappy's photo mode button on the pause screen. It opens photo mode while in a world.
snappy.options.buttons_disabled_warning: When both buttons are disabled, Snappy's options screen can only be opened through Mod Menu's Mods menu on Fabric or NeoForge's Mods menu on NeoForge.

snappy.capture.sun_warning.title: Sun-facing panorama warning
snappy.capture.sun_warning.message: Taking panorama screenshots while facing the sun can give the panorama a wrongly tinted cube face, because many shaders tint the view orange or red when facing the sun at specific times of day. Look away from the sun while taking panorama screenshots to avoid this.

snappy.photo_mode.title: Photo Mode
snappy.photo_mode.unavailable: Photo mode can only be used while in a world.
snappy.photo_mode.pause.desc: Pauses or unpauses the integrated singleplayer game while photo mode stays usable.
snappy.photo_mode.pause.unavailable_serv: Photo mode pausing is unavailable because you are on a server.
snappy.photo_mode.grid.desc: Shows a translucent rule-of-thirds grid over the photo view.
snappy.photo_mode.vignette.desc: Darkens the edges of the view so the center draws more attention. Keep it low for a subtle camera feel, or raise it for a stronger cinematic frame.
snappy.photo_mode.depth_of_field.desc: Turns on a camera-style blur that keeps your chosen focus area sharp while nearer or farther parts of the scene soften. Great for portraits, close-ups, and cinematic shots.
snappy.photo_mode.dof_focus_distance.des: Sets how far from the camera the sharpest point should be. Move it until your subject is clear; objects much nearer or farther away will blur.
snappy.photo_mode.dof_focal_length.desc: Changes how strongly the lens separates your subject from the background. Higher values make the focused area feel tighter and the blur more dramatic.
snappy.photo_mode.dof_aperture.desc: Controls how wide the virtual lens opens. Lower numbers create stronger blur and softer backgrounds; higher numbers keep more of the scene clear.
snappy.photo_mode.gamma.desc: Brightens or darkens the midtones after Minecraft's own brightness setting. Raise it to reveal more detail in darker areas; lower it for deeper, moodier shadows.
snappy.photo_mode.saturation.desc: Controls how intense the colors feel. Lower values fade the image toward gray; higher values make colors richer and livelier.
snappy.photo_mode.contrast.desc: Controls the separation between dark and bright areas. Lower values soften the image; higher values add punch and shape, but can hide some shadow detail.
snappy.photo_mode.overexposure.desc: Controls how strongly light is pushed across the image. Raise it for brighter, glowing highlights; lower it for a darker, more restrained look.
snappy.photo_mode.bloom.desc: Adds a soft glow around bright areas like sunlight, torches, reflections, and glowing blocks. Use a low value for a gentle cinematic shine, or raise it for a dreamier, more radiant shot.
snappy.photo_mode.film_grain.desc: Adds fine camera-style texture over the finished image, with stronger grain in darker tones and cleaner highlights. Use a low value for subtle photographic character, or raise it for a rougher film-stock look.
snappy.photo_mode.chromatic_aberration.d: Adds subtle red and blue lens separation near the edges of the frame. Keep it low for cinematic lens character, or raise it for a stronger distorted-camera look.
snappy.photo_mode.colorize.desc: Applies a finished color preset over the photo view. Use it to quickly change the mood, then fine-tune the result with the nearby color sliders.
snappy.photo_mode.stylize.desc: Changes the whole view into a specific style. Choose None for the normal look, or pick a style when you want the shot to feel more hand-drawn for example.
snappy.photo_mode.pose.desc: Select a pose for your player.
snappy.photo_mode.pose_maker.title: Pose Maker
snappy.photo_mode.pose_maker.model_y_off: Moves the whole posed player model up or down in blocks.
snappy.photo_mode.pose_maker.part.head: Head
snappy.photo_mode.armor.desc: Controls which armor slots are visible on your player in photo mode.
snappy.photo_mode.held_items.desc: Controls which held items are visible on your player in photo mode.
snappy.photo_mode.time.desc: Changes the rendered sky and lighting without changing the world's real time.
snappy.photo_mode.weather.desc: Changes rendered weather without changing the world's real weather.
snappy.photo_mode.force_biome_precipitat: Allows photo-mode rain and snow to render in biomes that normally hide precipitation.
snappy.photo_mode.season.desc: Visually changes snow, precipitation type, and seasonal plant colors while photo mode is active.
snappy.photo_mode.beacon_beams.desc: Controls whether beacon beams are visible while photo mode is active.
snappy.photo_mode.return_to_player.desc: Moves the photo camera back to its player-facing starting position without changing photo settings.
snappy.photo_mode.hide_gui.desc: Hide the photo mode interface. Press %s to bring it back.
snappy.photo_mode.confirm.hide_gui.title: Hide Photo Mode UI?
snappy.photo_mode.confirm.hide_gui.messa: This will hide the full photo mode interface. Press %s to bring it back.
snappy.photo_mode.confirm.reset.title: Reset Photo Mode?
snappy.photo_mode.confirm.reset.message: This will restore all settings to their defaults.
snappy.photo_mode.confirm.leave.title: Leave Photo Mode?
snappy.photo_mode.confirm.leave.message: Close photo mode and return to normal gameplay.
snappy.photo_mode.screenshot.unavailable: Photo mode screenshots can only be taken while in a world.
